CLUSTER 281
An Efficient Synthesis of Allenyl Perfluoroalkyl Ketones from 
Mono-1,2-Addition–Elimination Reaction of Allenoates with RfMgX
Synthesis of All enyl  Perfl uoroal kyl  Ket onesGuangke He, Can Xue, Chunling Fu, Shengming Ma*
Laboratory of Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, 
Hangzhou 310027, Zhejiang, P. R. of China
Fax +86(21)62609305; E-mail: masm@mail.sioc.ac.cn
Received 7 August 2009
SYNLETT 2010, No. 2, pp 0281–0285xx .xx .20 10
Advanced online publication: 04.01.2010
DOI: 10.1055/s-0029-1219169; Art ID: Y01709ST
© Georg Thieme Verlag Stuttgart · New York
Abstract: An efficient method for the synthesis of perfluoroalkyl
allenyl ketones via the 1,2-addition–elimination reaction of per-
fluoroalkyl Grignard reagents with allenoates has been established.
No further reaction was observed between these perfluoroalkyl ke-
tones and R
fMgX. Under the catalysis of PdCl 2 or AuCl3, perfluo-
roalkyl 1,2-allenyl ketones can be transformed to 2-perfluoroalkyl-
substituted furans; they may also undergo 1,2-addition with organ-
olithiums to afford tertiary 1,2-allenols containing a perfluoroalkyl
group.
Key words: 1,2-addition, elimination, allenoates, allenyl ketones,
Grignard reagents, cyclization
It is well known that the reaction of carboxylates with
Grignard reagents usually affords tertiary alcohols via the
intermediacy of ketones and it is very difficult to stop at
the stage of ketones.
1 Recently we have reported the
Fe(III)-catalyzed conjugate addition reaction of 2,3-allen-
oates with Grignard reagents affording 3-( Z)-alkenoates
highly regio- and stereoselectively.2 However, when allyl-
ic Grignard reagents were used tertiary 2,3-allenols were
formed.
3 Thus, we showed interest in the reaction of 2,3-
allenoates with RfMgX in the presence of Fe(III) catalyst.
In this paper, we wish to disclose our recent observation
that the reaction of allenoates with perfluoroalkyl Gri-
gnard reagents afforded allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketones,
which may be used for the synthesis of a variety of differ-
ent synthetically attractive products (Scheme 1).
Scheme 1
n-C4F9MgX was prepared by the I–Mg exchange reaction
of n-C4F9I with PhMgBr  in anhydrous Et 2O at –80 °C. 4
The reaction of methyl 2-methyl-4-phenyl-2,3-butadi-
enoate (1a) with this prepared Grignard reagent at –70 °C
in the presence of Fe(acac)3 (5% mol)2 afforded 4-phenyl-
2,3-butadien-2-yl perfluorobutyl ketone ( 2a) in 48%
NMR yield (entry 1, Table 1). The reaction in the absence
of Fe(acac)
3 afforded 2a in a much higher yield (entry 2,
Table 1). It should be noted that the tertiary alcohol 3a,
1,4-conjugate addition product 4a, and the 1,4-conjugate
addition-1,2-addition products 5a and 6a were not formed
as judged by the analysis of the NMR spectrum of the
crude product.
After literature searching, we noticed that Haszeldine et
al.
5 reported the reaction of R fMgX (R f = n-C3F7) with
RCO2Et (R = Me, Et, n-Pr, CF3, C2F5) afforded the mix-
tures of secondary alcohols, ketones, and tertiary alco-
hols; Ando et al.
6 recently reported the synthesis of two a-
aminoalkyl perfluoroalkyl ketones from the reaction of N-
Boc-L-phenylalanine methyl ester with R fMgX (R f =
n-C4F9). In addition, he also reported that the reaction of
(4R,5R)-2,2-dimethyl-1,3-dioxolane-4,5-dicarboxylate with
RfMgX (Rf = n-C4F9 or n-C8F17) affords the products with
one carboxylate being converted to bisperfluoroalkyl-sub-
stituted tertiary alcohol and the other being converted to
perfluoroalkyl ketone.
7 Furthermore, it is interesting to
note that no reaction was observed in THF (entry 3,
Table 1); The reaction with 3.0 equivalents of the Grig-
nard reagents led to an incomplete conversion (entries 3–
6, Table 1); even with n-C
4F9Ti(OPr-i)4MgBr, the reac-
tion afforded ketone 2a in 47% yield (entry 7, Table 1); 8
the yield for the reaction with ethyl 2-methyl-4-phenyl-
2,3-butadienoate ( 1b) is relatively higher than that with
the methyl ester (entry 8, Table 1).
As we know that perfluoroalkyl ketones9–12 are important
in organic synthesis, pharmaceutical industry, and materi-
al science, and both starting materials are easily avail-
able,
13,14 we started to explore the scope of this reaction
(Table 2). Differently substituted 2,3-allenoates, such as
2-monosubstituted (entries 8 and 9, Table 2), 2,4- (entries
1–7, Table 2), or 4,4-disubstituted (entry 10, Table 2), and
full-substituted allenoates (entries 11–15, Table 2) may
all undergo this transformation to afford the 1,2-allenyl
perfluoroalkyl ketones in moderate yields.
The reaction may also be extended to 4,5-dodecadienoate
(1k, Equation 1).

The resulting 1,2-allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketone 2a was ob-
served to be stable even up to room temperature towards
n-C
4F9MgX, explaining the results observed (Scheme 2).
Scheme 2
These 1,2-allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketones have been dem-
onstrated to be useful intermediates in organic synthesis
as shown in Scheme 3. The reaction of 2a with MeMgCl
afforded 1-perfluoroalkyl-2,3-allenols 7a in a low NMR
yield (41%); however, the reaction of 2a with MeLi or n-
BuLi afforded the 1,2-addition products 7a and 7b in 80%
and 70% yields, respectively. 2-Perfluoroalkyl-substitut-
ed furans 8a and 8b may be formed in the presence (with
5 mol% PdCl
2)16,17 and absence (with 5 mol% AuCl3)18,19
of allyl bromide (5 equiv), respectively.
In conclusion, we have developed an efficient synthesis of
allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketones from the reaction of allen-
oates with perfluoroalkyl Grignard reagents, which is very
different from the normal reaction of carboxylates with
classic Grignard reagents. Due to the easy availability of
the starting materials and the potential of the products, this
reaction will be very useful for the introduction of perflu-
oroalkyl group into a variety of different organic skele-
tons. Further studies in this area are being pursued in our
laboratory.
Acknowledgment
Financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of
China (No. 20732005) and the Major State Basic Research De-
velopment Program (No. G2006CB806105) is greatly appreciated.
Shengming Ma is a Qiu Shi Adjunct Professor at Zhejiang Univer-
sity, who enjoys spending the weekend in Hangzhou with some
exercise.

(15) Method A
To a dried Schlenk tube were added n-C
4F9I (0.36 mL, 
d = 2.01 g/mL, 0.72 g, 2.09 mmol) and anhyd Et2O (2.5 mL). 
The resulting mixture was cooled to –80 °C in a cooling bath 
and a solution of EtMgBr (0.47 mL, 3.0 M in Et2O, 1.41 
mmol) was added dropwise at –80 °C with stirring. After the 
addition, anhyd Et2O (0.7 mL) was used to rinse the 
remaining EtMgBr. The resulting mixture was stirred for 70 
min at this temperature. A solution of 1b (81.0 mg, 0.40 
mmol) in anhyd Et2O (1 mL) was added dropwise at –80 °C 
with stirring. Then the mixture was allowed to warm up to 
–70 °C within 30 min and stirred at –70 °C for 6 h. The 
mixture was quenched with 5 mL of a sat. aq NH
4Cl solution 
at –70 °C. After being warmed up to r.t. naturally, the 
mixture was extracted with Et2O (3 × 20 mL). The combined 
organic extracts were washed with brine (5 mL) and dried 
over anhyd Na2SO4. Filtration, evaporation, and 
chromatography on silica gel [eluent: petroleum ether (bp 
60–90 °C)] afforded 2a (111.0 mg, 74%) as a liquid.
